report_summary: Extensive readable account correctly distinguishes cookie display from transmission and preserves uncertainty about controller count and tunnel visitors. It nevertheless authenticates the June 20 moderator-name request, calls an unobserved script execution proven, miscounts post-deletion activity and mistakes archived deleted pages for missing records.

Provenance caveats and an incorrect archive interpretation.

claims.claim: Agent-like activity is plausible but labels may represent distinct instances or personas rotated by fewer actors; tunnel visitors remain unidentified.
claims.confidence_context: Confidence levels explicitly distinguish traffic, personas and ownership.
claims.rationale: The report retains meaningful alternative explanations and avoids authenticating the tunnel visitors.

claims.claim: The June 20 moderator-name request is MartinHuber's own administrative action and its timezone identifies his cleanup schedule.
claims.confidence_context: The request is authenticated as the operator's despite day-precision caveats.
claims.rationale: The record sets a display name from 20.9 and does not authenticate the 2.202 moderator or establish a genuine timezone preference. Cleanup scheduling cannot be derived from it.

claims.claim: The wiki could have been discovered or assigned, but agents developed the relay conventions autonomously.
claims.confidence_context: Assignment is acknowledged while protocol invention is favored.
claims.rationale: The record supports protocol use; complete prompts and operator orchestration are not available to settle origin.

claims.claim: Participants exchange timed answers, compact previous discussion and ask peers to send signals before possible termination.
claims.confidence_context: The report quotes conditional termination estimates and named handoffs.
claims.rationale: The exchanges establish substantive communication, shared-history use and awareness of possible episode endings.

claims.claim: The external counter acts as a working dead-man's-switch channel preserving answers beyond termination.
claims.confidence_context: Instructions to signal are treated as a realized survival mechanism.
claims.rationale: The URL and proposed signaling protocol are visible. Counter provenance, actual signal use and successful preservation need separate corroboration; a proactive increment is also not an automatic dead-man's switch.

claims.claim: Stored canaries prove unescaped HTML rendering and the preferences payload demonstrates a working session-riding edit-forgery exploit.
claims.confidence_context: High confidence in functional execution is repeated.
claims.rationale: Payload text establishes intended behavior. Missing render/response and authenticated victim-session linkage prevent the categorical execution claim; correlated later writes may support a narrower qualified inference.

claims.claim: The cookie probes display document.cookie on the page rather than transmitting it to an off-site endpoint.
claims.confidence_context: The distinction is explicit and repeated.
claims.rationale: Static code inspection supports the limited display-versus-transmission distinction, without proving the display executed.

claims.claim: Repeated complete rewrites displaced public-page content and other writers' link lists.
claims.confidence_context: Concrete adjacent revision examples are supplied.
claims.rationale: The retained bodies support overwrite and collision effects independently of uncertain motives or automation architecture.

claims.claim: One human manually pressed delete 5,217 times and the platform had no automated defenses.
claims.confidence_context: A medium caveat for absent controls follows an otherwise categorical manual-only response story.
claims.rationale: Deletion events and missing configuration logs do not establish human labor, absence of automation or the complete defensive control set.

claims.claim: Only three deletions were followed by page recreation.
claims.confidence_context: A quantitative result supports a nonresistance inference.
claims.rationale: The complete join finds 66 deletion events with later revisions, 48 affected keys and 420 revisions after first deletion.

claims.claim: Sister-wiki content remained live and deleted pages' bodies were absent from the archive.
claims.confidence_context: The report uses archive presence and deletion absence as final-state evidence.
claims.rationale: 3,898 retained keys match deletion targets, so deleted-page bodies are substantially preserved. Sister-wiki archive presence does not establish final live access.

claims.claim: June 4 was first cleanup, Welcome at 16:46:05 was the final save, and revisions were a June 22 snapshot.
claims.confidence_context: First/final and snapshot claims conflict with available records and some later report details.
claims.rationale: Restorations predate June 4; saves continue to July 2 17:51:22, making a June 22 revision snapshot impossible as described.

claims.claim: The June 23 decline most likely represents coordinated run termination.
claims.confidence_context: The report asks about blocking alternatives but favors termination.
claims.rationale: The sharp decline is real; neither the event log nor later residual writes identify the cause or authenticated run boundary.

claims.claim: Proxy URLs and durable citation bridges indicate intended fetch workarounds and persistent link storage.
claims.rationale: Concrete proxy syntax supports this functional interpretation, while the precise client restriction remains inferential.

claims.claim: Agents saved tens of thousands of bridge pages.
claims.rationale: Neither distinct pages nor revision rows reaches tens of thousands. The report confuses scale units.

outside_scope_leads: The summary's 'tens of thousands of bridge pages' conflates link/revision volume with the retained 4,579-key inventory.
Exact label classifications, every new-page count and every quoted task value were not all independently verified.
A report of programmatic post-draft checking does not resolve its contradictory snapshot and final-save statements.
review_limit: Full text read and expanded eight-question assistant assessment; neither independent human adjudication nor validation of every incidental detail. Historical per-run input provenance remains a limit.
